Title: Whitebark Pines in Yellowstone Park
Content: Scientists claim that mountain pine beetles have been blamed for the death of mature whitebark pine trees in the Greater Yellowstone forest ecosystem. The beetles burrow into the trees to lay their eggs. When the eggs hatch, the larvae feed on the tree, cutting off the flow of water. As a result, the trees become stressed and begin to die. An increase in the temperature is contributing to the increase in beetles. Cooler temperatures tend to keep the beetle population controlled. Many organisms, including squirrels, birds, and even grizzly bears, have been impacted by the decrease in the numbers of trees. Many organisms use whitebark pine seeds for food.
